items.title: The Florida Times-Union’s Demetrius Harvey reports Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) was not seen at practice Wednesday.
items.text: Tuten was banged up last week against the Giants and clearly playing through considerable discomfort. That he hasn’t practiced much over the past couple weeks means Tuten could sit out a couple days of practice this week and still suit up for Week 12 against the Titans. The Jaguars would do well to rest their lead back in a game they should win comfortably. Chris Rodriguez, who bests Tuten in rushing success rate, rush yards over expected per attempt, and EPA per rush, would be in line for a big workload if Tuten is held out in Week 12. - Denny Carter

items.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Ken Walker (groin) is out for Week 12 against the Bills.
items.text: Walker was always going to be a long shot to suit up for KC’s Thanksgiving night game against Buffalo. This will be the third straight game in which Walker has been sidelined, leaving Emmett Johnson as the team’s workhorse back for at least one more week. Johnson over the past two weeks is fourth in rush yards, ninth in explosive run rate, 14th in rush yards over expected per attempt, and fourth in missed tackles forced per attempt. In other words, he’s good. Johnson will be a top-10 option against the Bills. - Denny Carter

items.title: Colts DE Caden Curry (wrist) is out for the season.
items.text: Curry suffered the injury last week and will be sidelined for the rest of the season. His absence will be yet another blow for a crumbling Colts defense that has been bludgeoned over the past few weeks through the air and on the ground. Curry had 14 tackles and one tackle for loss over 11 games. - Denny Carter

items.title: Bucs opened the 21-day practice window for Jalen McMillan (knee).
items.text: McMillan has been on injured reserve since late September with a PCL injury. His practice window opening today could mean McMillan will suit up in Week 12 against the Panthers. He would not be a fantasy option for now in a run-first Tampa offense with several wideouts ahead of McMillan in the pass-catching pecking order. - Denny Carter

items.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said he expected the Bills offense to be “more complex” in Week 12 against the Chiefs.
items.text: Fowler suggested the Bills kept the game plan as simple as possible last week against the inferior Dolphins, with Josh Allen throwing 45 passes from the pocket and failing to log a single rushing attempt after averaging 7.1 rushes per game coming into Week 11. Fowler said the Bills might have wanted to hide offensive wrinkles ahead of their Thanksgiving night matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. items.title: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo said it “sounds like” the benching of Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph was “not a popular decision in the locker room.”
items.text: Rodgers was reportedly excused from meetings at the team facility on Wednesday, two days ahead of the Steelers’ Week 12 game against Denver. Rodgers’ benching comes after a series of down games and a proposed change from Rodgers about how plays are communicated to him during the game. Rudolph could be a slight upgrade for Pittsburgh pass catchers and should be rostered in supeflex formats for now. - Denny Carter

items.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Rodgers was excused from a Wednesday morning meeting.
items.text: Schefter said the veteran was excused from showing up Wednesday morning so he could “process” being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for Week 12 against the Broncos. That seems fair. Whatever happens from here, Rodgers has certainly taken his last snap as a Steeler. Rudolph, meanwhile, should be rostered in all superflex leagues for now. - Denny Carter

items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers.
items.text: Rapoport said McCarthy’s decision came after extensive meetings with coaches, players, and Rodgers himself following the Steelers’ Week 11 loss to the Joe Milton-led Eagles. Mason Rudolph is slated to get the start in Week 12 against the Broncos. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said the team was set to make a change in play calling, with QB coach Tom Arth relaying plays to Rodgers on game days “at the behest of Rodgers.” Hours later, the 42-year-old veteran was benched. items.title: The Steelers have named Mason Rudolph their starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.text: The news of Aaron Rodgers’ benching and Rudolph’s sudden promotion came in an 11:10 PM ET Tuesday evening press release. Normal stuff. While we wait for the next shoe to drop on the “Rodgers situation,” we can begin evaluating the “Rudolph development.” In short: Not much will change, though Rodgers’ recent immobility and subsequent inaccuracy had reached a boiling point. items.title: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.text: 42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worse of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest.
